title: Sliding Window Maximum
source: canonical Sliding Window Maximum concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is an array of integers nums and a window width k. Slide a window of k consecutive elements across nums from left to right, one position at a time. Return one value per window position: the largest element inside that window.
hints: Recomputing the maximum of every window from scratch repeats comparisons across overlapping windows.
A window maximum only stops mattering when it leaves the window, and a new element only matters if it is bigger than smaller elements still inside.
Keep a deque of indices with decreasing values: pop smaller values from the back when a new element arrives, drop the front when it slides out of range, and read the front as the window maximum.
solution: Monotonic deque of indices holding values in decreasing order. Each element is pushed once, evicting smaller values that can never be a future maximum; the front index is evicted when it leaves the window. Every index enters and leaves the deque once: O(n) time, O(k) space.
bruteForceCode:
def max_sliding_window(nums, k):
    return [max(nums[i:i + k]) for i in range(len(nums) - k + 1)]
failureHint: hidden tests include k = 1, k = len(nums), decreasing runs, and negative values
